edits.name: Scheduled-jobs registry in family.json5: per-person switches, a charter per job, failure guardrails
edits.description: Every scheduled feature becomes a named switch per person in one reviewed file. From that entry the generator creates the job with a time limit and a tool cap and writes a short charter the parents can read: what Happy may do without asking, what needs a yes first, when to stop and ask, what it must never do. Failures alert Tony, not the family; a job that keeps failing stops itself; runs missed during a power cut are skipped.
edits.example: Turning Jordan's school digest off is a one-line change Tony reviews. The 19:30 brief fails twice in a row: Tony gets one text, and one more when it recovers. After a power cut the 07:00 brief does not turn up at 11:40.
edits.how: gen-family reads the family.json5 flags and emits `openclaw automations add/edit/remove`, keyed on the stable `--name`, with `--agent`, `--to`, `--tz`, `--announce`, `--timeout-seconds` and an explicit `--tools` cap on every job; it diffs against `automations list --all --json`, because the default list hides disabled jobs. The same entries render one `## Program: <name>` section per job (Authority, Trigger, Approval gate, Escalation, What NOT to do, plus an execute-verify-report rule) into templates/person/AGENTS.md, and each job message points at its program instead of repeating it; isolated jobs must not use `--light-context`, which drops the bootstrap files. Gateway config: a global `cron.failureAlert` object routed to the operator's handle; `cron.skipMissedJobs: true`; `cron.triggers.enabled: false`, set before any agent is given the `automations` tool. happy-inspect reads `automations list --all` to catch auto-disabled jobs. The healthchecks dead-man switch stays the only signal for a Mac that is off.
caveats: A charter is prompt text, not enforcement; the hard limits stay in tool policy and hooks.

AGENTS.md shares a bootstrap budget (20,000 characters per file by default); keep each program to about ten lines. Scheduled runs do not get MEMORY.md, so anything a program needs must be in AGENTS.md, the job message or a tool result.
A chat instruction does not change a charter; it waits for a reviewed deploy.
By default a failure alert goes to the failing job's own announce target, so Jordan would get 'job failed' texts for her jobs unless they are rerouted to Tony.
Alerts start after 2 failures in a row with a 1-hour cooldown. A recurring job is switched off after 10 failures in a row and then disappears from the default job list.
Without a per-job timeout an isolated agent job is bounded only by a 60-minute watchdog.
After a reboot with FileVault locked nothing fires and nothing alerts. One-shot reminders still catch up after an outage even with skipMissedJobs set.

Jobs an agent creates in chat, once

-main holds the automations tool, are outside the registry, so the diff must tolerate or report them.

With triggers on, trigger scripts and script payloads run with the owning agent's full tool policy, exec included. Switching triggers off also switches off the trigger-script design of F029 until that is deliberately turned back on.
edits.safety: Purely restrictive. Charters narrow behaviour and grant nothing; never-list items are written under What NOT to do and are also unreachable by tool policy. Alert text shown in chat is a normalized cause, and routing alerts to the operator keeps one person's job details out of another person's thread.

edits.how: In-house plugin. before_dispatch claims the exact phrase from an adult's handle and writes a kill file (everything) or a suspended file (one person's handles). The stop is enforced where hooks fail closed: before_agent_run blocks agent runs before the model reads the prompt, and before_tool_call blocks tools; message_sending cancels scheduled announce texts as a best-effort extra. Levels that need no plugin code, done by Tony: `cron.enabled: false`, then `openclaw gateway stop`. Lifting a stop or a lock-out is CLI-only. For a stolen phone the operator step still has to follow: remove the handle from family.json5 and redeploy, which is the only thing that ends that handle's approver rights; `openclaw devices revoke` if the phone ran the OpenClaw app; Find My Lost Mode on the phone side.
